author: reek
body: 200 visible against a 264-pixel scanline is the same shape small, and no emulator feature is involved because the stride is an ordinary argument.

author: reek
body: The discriminator does not depend on which pixels a glyph happens to set, which matters because a test that assumed a particular bitmap would be asserting about the font instead of about the stride. Every painted pixel is counted twice: once over the whole buffer, and once inside the box the subject was asked to paint, addressed by stride. A stride-stepping walk puts all of them inside the box. A width-stepping walk leaves row 0 there and scatters every later row, because row r lands at r * 200 instead of r * 264, so the two counts stop agreeing. Anything drawn at all satisfies the first count, which is why the pair is the assertion and neither half is.

author: reek
body: The last row is the calibration and it is the reason to believe the rest: the same text is drawn into a fresh buffer with the visible width handed in as the pitch, and the counts are required to DISAGREE. Without it every row above would be satisfied by a subject that painted nothing outside its box because it painted almost nothing at all.

author: reek
body: Sabotaged against seed 6671C19A0F78F630 by giving `comp-draw-node`'s WkPanel arm the node's own width as the pitch: `draw-node rows by stride` and `render inside the panel` go to `no`, and the three text rows and the calibration hold. The painted rows stay `yes` under it, which is the point of keeping them -- the defect moves where the pixels went, not whether there were any.

author: reek
body: Every non-zero word in the buffer, wherever it landed. Walking the raw extent rather than the rows on purpose: a width-stepping painter writes outside every row this test knows about, and a counter that only visited the rows would miss exactly the pixels that prove the defect.
